task.title: Android app controls are trapped under the system status and nav bars
task.description:
Maintainer report with screenshot (2026-08-16, release APK on a real phone): every control in the app's top bar and bottom tab bar is unreachable — overlapped by the native Android status bar (top) and gesture/navigation bar (bottom). This blocks testing sign-in on device (the login affordance lives in the top bar) and makes mode switching impossible.

Mechanism (verify): the Android project targets SDK 36 (gen/android/app/build.gradle.kts), and Android 15+ ENFORCES edge-to-edge for targetSdk >= 35 — the WebView draws behind the system bars. The web shell's fixed header and bottom_nav apply no safe-area padding, and the SSR viewport meta is plain 'width=device-width, initial-scale=1' (no viewport-fit=cover).

Candidate fixes, smallest-honest first: (a) native-side — apply WindowInsets as padding/margins to the WebView in the generated MainActivity (or windowOptOutEdgeToEdgeEnforcement=true in the manifest as an explicitly-temporary Android opt-out that Google will remove); (b) web-side — viewport-fit=cover + env(safe-area-inset-top/bottom) padding on the shell's header and the mobile tab bar (check Android WebView actually reports env() insets under enforced edge-to-edge; iOS/WKWebView would want the same treatment eventually). Whichever ships, the mobile shell (design/information-architecture.md 'Mobile shell') and specs/app-ui.md get the ruling. Verify on the emulator via android-smoke (dev webview attach can measure the tab bar's bounding box vs the visual viewport) AND note edge-to-edge enforcement may differ between emulator API level and the maintainer's phone — match API levels or verify on both. Gen-android files are tauri-generated but repo-committed; edits there are legitimate (the signing config precedent) but must survive regeneration — note the tradeoff in the report.
